description: Player-controller feel and body geometry for the isometric adaptation. Canonical numbers (walk and climb speed, the Speed/Jump caps, the jump-height table, the gravity and upward speed of MeowDB's knockback model) are NOT repeated here: MovementModel reads them from data/canonical/formulas/movement.json and converts them with WorldScale. This file holds only values MeowDB does not publish or that the 3D adaptation needs. Every key has a reason under 'reasons'. Owner: the player controller (docs/runtime/PLAYER_AND_CAMERA.md).

reasons.gravity: Not stored here: the controller uses MeowDB's knockback-model gravity (canonical knockback_airtime.gravity_px_per_s2 = 2000 px/s^2, x WorldScale.v = 23.4 m/s^2) for jumps too, so jumps and knockback share one arc. With the canonical 77 px apex at Jump 100 this implies a launch speed of sqrt(2 x 2000 x 77) = 555 px/s and 0.555 s of same-height airtime, and the same rule reproduces every row of MeowDB's jump table (launch speed proportional to Jump: 111 px at Jump 120). A floatier gravity would read as 'realistic' and slow; this keeps the hop short and snappy like classic.
reasons.body_height_m: Iteration One's player proxy and every route/collision rule assume a 1.5 m chibi body (traversal BODY_Z 0.15-1.5 m).
reasons.body_radius_m: 0.6 m wide capsule: matches the chibi proxy's shoulders and passes the exporter's 0.45 m prop clearance from route centrelines. The collision capsule covers the body from step_up_m to body_height_m (the band below is the step band, sensed by the feet rays).
reasons.foot_radius_m: The feet are a disc of 9 downward rays (centre + 8 at this radius). The player stands on the highest walkable hit, so a ledge or step is mounted when the front of the feet reaches it, and the player falls off an edge once the centre is 0.15 m past it (classic: you drop when your feet leave the foothold). Half the body radius, so the body never hangs visibly over a drop.
reasons.ground_accel_mps2: MeowDB gap (walking acceleration is undocumented). MapleStory feel is immediate: 60 m/s^2 reaches the 3.0 m/s walk speed in 0.05 s (3 physics ticks), which reads as instant without a one-frame snap.
reasons.ground_decel_mps2: MeowDB gap. Stops from walk speed in 0.033 s (2 ticks): fast to stop, no slide.
reasons.air_accel_mps2: MeowDB gap (air control undocumented). Classic-limited: momentum is kept when no key is held, and steering changes horizontal speed at 6 m/s^2, so a full reversal from walk speed takes 1.0 s (almost twice a 0.555 s jump: a running jump can be shortened, not turned around) while a standing jump can still drift up to ~0.9 m. Responsive enough to correct a jump, never a mid-air U-turn.
reasons.max_fall_speed_mps: MeowDB gap (no published terminal fall speed). 12 m/s keeps long drops readable from the isometric camera and stays above 500 px/s x WorldScale.v (5.85 m/s), the fast-fall threshold of MeowDB's fall-damage counter, so that rule stays reachable if fall damage is ever enabled.
reasons.coyote_time_s: Adaptation (not a classic mechanic): a jump pressed within 0.08 s (5 ticks) of walking off an edge still fires. The isometric view makes the exact edge hard to judge; this forgives that without changing jump height.
reasons.jump_buffer_s: Adaptation: a jump pressed up to 0.12 s before landing fires on landing, so a slightly early press is not lost.
reasons.hold_to_rejump: Classic behaviour: holding the jump key keeps hopping on every landing.
reasons.step_up_m: Largest ledge/stair riser walked without jumping. Equals Iteration One's traversal MAX_STEP (0.45 m), which every exported route was validated against. The same band applies when landing a jump, so the highest reachable ledge is jump apex + step_up_m (1.35 m at Jump 100): one classic platform tier plus a forgiving margin, exactly the reach MAP_ARCHITECTURE section 4.4 budgets (jump_apex_m_at_cap + step_up_m) for the one-way ledge. MAP_ARCHITECTURE reads this key.
reasons.floor_max_angle_deg: Steepest walkable slope; equals Iteration One's MAX_SLOPE_DEG (38) used by traversal.py and trails.py.
reasons.snap_down_m: How far the body sticks to the ground per tick when walking down stairs, ramps and small ledges (one step_up). A larger drop is a fall.
reasons.jump_apex_m_at_cap: DERIVED, not tuned: canonical jump_height_px_by_jump at Jump 120 (111 px) x WorldScale.v (0.0117) = 1.2987 m. Kept here because MAP_ARCHITECTURE section 4.4 (the 30 -> 40 ledge invariant) and the L1 flood fill read it; test_player_movement_model pins it to the derivation.
reasons.teleport_settle_m: teleport() lowers the body onto ground found within this distance below the arrival point, so is_on_floor() is true on the first tick (MAP_ARCHITECTURE section 4.5 ARRIVING allows 10 frames).
reasons.climb_grab_radius_m: Horizontal distance from a ladder/rope line within which Up (portal_enter) or interact grabs it. Tight enough that a ladder beside a portal does not steal the press.
reasons.climb_top_grab_radius_m: Distance from a climbable's top exit within which Down (climb_down) or interact grabs it from above.
reasons.climb_standoff_m: The body hangs this far in front of the ladder/rope line (toward the camera side), so the capsule never overlaps the cliff face behind it.
reasons.climb_exit_below_top_m: Climbing up ends (onto top_exit) when the feet are this close below the climbable's top; the visual offset smooths the last step.
reasons.climb_jump_off_apex_fraction: Jumping sideways off a rope/ladder is a smaller hop than a ground jump (half the apex), so it reads as letting go rather than a full jump.
reasons.climb_regrab_cooldown_s: After letting go, the same press cannot immediately re-grab, so a jump-off is not undone by a held Up.
reasons.knockback_horizontal_speed_mps: MeowDB gap: MeowDB's knockback model documents only the vertical part (270 px/s up, 2000 px/s^2, 0.27 s airtime). The horizontal push is an adaptation: 2.2 m/s over ~0.27 s of airtime moves the player ~0.6 m, a readable shove of about one body width that rarely carries the player off a ledge.
reasons.knockback_max_hitstun_s: Hit-stun (no input) lasts until the knockback arc lands, at most this long, so a knockback off a ledge does not lock input for the whole fall. MeowDB: the airtime model 'does not measure how long you lose the ability to attack'.
reasons.visual_step_smoothing_s: Presentation only: the body steps up/down a riser in one tick, the model eases over this time so stairs and ladder exits do not pop.
reasons.facing_turn_rate_deg_per_s: Presentation only: the model turns to the facing direction at this rate (a 180 degree turn takes 0.125 s). Logical facing is instant.
